explain.say: A building's carbon has a life story. Look at the stages: making the materials, building, years of use with heating and lighting, demolition, and finally credit for reuse. Embodied carbon is everything except the energy used to run the building, which is operational carbon. As buildings get better insulated, which share do you think grows?

explain.say: Embodied carbon! Now compare per kilogram: steel about one point five five, cement about zero point nine one, concrete only about zero point one three. But we use enormous amounts of concrete. A hundred cubic metre slab weighs two hundred and forty tonnes, so it carries about thirty one tonnes of carbon dioxide.

items.label: Cement
items.ask: Why is cement so carbon intensive?

explain.say: Why is cement so bad? Heating limestone to make it releases carbon dioxide straight from the rock, besides the fuel burned. So engineers swap part of the cement for slag or fly ash, use timber where it suits, and recycled steel. Rating systems like LEED, BREEAM and GRIHA score all of this. Which group would a timber frame fall in?

faq.a: The greenhouse gas emissions from making, transporting, building with, maintaining and finally disposing of a building's materials, as opposed to running it.
asks: What is embodied carbon in buildings?

faq.q: What is the difference between embodied and operational carbon?
faq.a: Operational carbon comes from the energy used to heat, cool and light a building in use. Embodied carbon is in the materials and construction. In well-insulated new buildings, embodied carbon can be half or more of the whole-life total.

faq.q: Why is cement so carbon intensive?
faq.a: Cement clinker is made by heating limestone to about 1,450 degrees Celsius. Burning fuel releases CO2, and the limestone itself gives off CO2 as it turns into lime, about one kilogram of CO2 per kilogram of Portland cement in total.
asks: Why is cement so bad for the climate?

faq.q: How do you calculate the embodied carbon of a concrete slab?
faq.a: Multiply the volume by the density and by a carbon factor. 100 cubic metres times 2,400 kilograms per cubic metre times about 0.13 kilograms of CO2e per kilogram gives about 31 tonnes.
asks: How do you calculate the embodied carbon of concrete?

faq.q: What are green building rating systems?
faq.a: Schemes that score buildings on energy, water, materials, carbon and wellbeing, such as LEED in the USA, BREEAM in the UK, GRIHA and IGBC in India, and Green Star in Australia.

facts: A 2018 Chatham House report estimated cement production causes about 8% of global CO₂ emissions.
The Inventory of Carbon and Energy (ICE) from the University of Bath is a widely used database of embodied carbon factors.

quiz.say: A slab uses 50 cubic metres of concrete weighing 2,400 kilograms per cubic metre, at 0.13 kilograms of CO2 per kilogram. What is its embodied carbon?
quiz.show: 50 m³ of concrete (2,400 kg/m³) at 0.13 kg CO₂e/kg. Embodied carbon?

wrong.1: That multiplies the volume by 0.13 and forgets the density.
wrong.2: That slips a factor of ten.

quiz.why: Operational carbon comes from energy used while the building runs.
